answer: A haven plot gates entry: the orchard registry auctions plots in sale order, one per identity, key-bound. The first plot costs a 40-credit bond; later plots cost 2 more each, so the k-th fake costs 40+2(k-1) credits and 1,000 fakes lock 1,039,000 credits, no bulk discount. Auditors recompute each price from the sale order and, before the horizon closes, require proof of key control; a mismatch burns the bond and revokes the identity. A rented-plot ring fails because one renter cannot prove control of many key-bound plots. An honest agent buys one plot for 40 credits once.
